title: Forbidden love
goal: Recognize the Persian izafet and the Arabic article in titles, fixed phrases and everyday adverbs.

intro.text: Ottoman Turkish could join two Persian or Arabic words head first: *aşk-ı memnu*, **forbidden love**, which modern Turkish says *yasak aşk*. Phrases that became ordinary words are written as one: *hüsnüniyet* (good faith). The Arabic article *al* hides inside *bilhassa* (especially) and *maalesef* (unfortunately).

exercises.question: What does the novel title *Aşk-ı Memnu* mean?

why.1: *Memnu* is not a name: it is an Arabic adjective, **forbidden**.
why.2: An izafet is a phrase, not a sentence: **forbidden love**.
why.3: *Memnu* is not a name, and in an izafet the second word describes the first.

exercises.explain: Head noun + *-ı* + modifier: *aşk-ı memnu* is *yasak aşk*, **forbidden love**.

exercises.question: How does the TDK dictionary write **good faith**?

why.1: The hyphen belongs to scholarly transcription and to titles such as *Aşk-ı Memnu*. Phrases that became ordinary words are written as one word.
why.2: The linking vowel belongs to the first noun, and the phrase is now a single word: *hüsnüniyet*.

exercises.explain: Izafets that became ordinary words are written as one word: *hüsnüniyet*, *devriâlem*, *suistimal*, *Babıali*.

accept: I have no doubt about his good intentions.
I have no doubt about his good faith.
I have no doubt about his goodwill.
I have no doubt about her [good intentions|good faith|goodwill].
I have no doubt of [his|her] [good intentions|good faith|goodwill].
I have no doubt at all [about|of] [his|her] [good intentions|good faith|goodwill].
I [do not|never] doubt [his|her] [good intentions|good faith|goodwill] (at all).
exercises.explain: *Hüsnüniyet* (good faith) + possessive + ablative: *hüsnüniyetinden*. *Şüphem yok* is **I have no doubt**.

exercises.en: I'm not tired; on the contrary, I feel very rested.

accept: bilakis
aksine

reject.why: *Bilhassa* is **especially**. **On the contrary** is *bilakis*: *bi-l-akis*, with the reverse.

exercises.explain: *Bilakis*: *bi* (with) + the article + *akis* (the reverse), **on the contrary**. Everyday synonyms: *aksine*, *tersine*.

Maalesef müdür kendisi gelemedi.
Ne yazık ki müdür [bizzat|kendisi] gelemedi.
Müdür [maalesef|ne yazık ki] [bizzat|kendisi] gelemedi.

exercises.explain: *Maalesef* (with the regret) and *bizzat* (by the self) both hide the Arabic article. *Kendisi gelemedi* says the same in plain Turkish.

exercises.title: Edebiyat dersinde
exercises.passage:
Edebiyat öğretmenimiz tahtaya iki kelime yazdı: “Aşk-ı Memnu”. Sonra sınıfa döndü: “Bu, Halit Ziya Uşaklıgil'in en ünlü romanının adı. Ne anlama geldiğini kim tahmin edebilir?”

Arka sıradan Can cevap verdi: “Memnu birinin adı mı? Belki romandaki kızın adıdır.”

Öğretmen gülümsedi: “Güzel bir tahmin, ama değil. Memnu Arapça bir sıfat, **yasak** demek. Osmanlıcada iki kelime Farsça kurala göre de birleşebilirdi: önce isim, sonra **-ı**, en son sıfat. Yani Aşk-ı Memnu, bugünkü Türkçeyle **yasak aşk**.”

Elif sordu: “Hocam, bilhassa da böyle mi kurulmuş? Babaannem bu kelimeyi çok kullanır.”

“O başka bir kurala örnek. Ortasında Arapçadaki **el** takısı var. Maalesef, bilakis, fevkalade gibi kelimeler de öyle. Bu kelimeleri tek tek öğrenmeniz yeterli; bu kurallarla yeni kelime yapmaya çalışmayın.”

glossary.en: to be formed, to be built

exercises.translation: Our literature teacher wrote two words on the board: “Aşk-ı Memnu”. Then she turned to the class: “This is the title of Halit Ziya Uşaklıgil's most famous novel. Who can guess what it means?” From the back row Can answered: “Is Memnu someone's name? Maybe it's the name of the girl in the novel.” The teacher smiled: “A good guess, but no. Memnu is an Arabic adjective; it means ‘forbidden’. In Ottoman Turkish two words could also be combined by a Persian rule: first the noun, then -ı, then the adjective. So Aşk-ı Memnu is ‘forbidden love’ in today's Turkish.” Elif asked: “Miss, is bilhassa formed like that too? My grandmother uses that word a lot.” “That's an example of another rule. In the middle of it there's the Arabic article, al. Words like maalesef, bilakis and fevkalade are the same. It's enough to learn these words one by one; don't try to make new words with these rules.”

questions.q: How does the teacher describe the word order of *Aşk-ı Memnu*?
options: Noun first, then -ı, then the adjective
questions.explain: *Önce isim, sonra -ı, en son sıfat*: the Persian izafet.

options: Her grandmother uses it a lot
It is in the novel's title
She saw it on the board
Learn these words one by one, without making new ones
Use the rules to build new words

exercises.text: Emekli olduktan sonra eşiyle bir ___ yapmayı planlıyor.
exercises.en: After he retires, he's planning a trip round the world with his wife.

accept: devriâlem

reject.why: That is the transcription of the Ottoman phrase. As an ordinary word, TDK writes it in one piece: *devriâlem*.

exercises.explain: *Devriâlem* (*devr-i âlem*, the turn of the world): an izafet that became a word, written as one. *Dünya turu* says the same in plain Turkish.

exercises.explain: *Ala-l-acele* (on the haste): **in a rush**. *Fevk-al-âde* (above the usual): **extraordinary**, and in praise **excellent**.

exercises.prompt: He abused his friends' good faith.
accept: Arkadaşlarının hüsnüniyetini suistimal etti.
Arkadaşlarının hüsnüniyetini kötüye kullandı.
Arkadaşlarının iyi niyetini [suistimal etti|kötüye kullandı].
Kendi arkadaşlarının [hüsnüniyetini|iyi niyetini] [suistimal etti|kötüye kullandı].
O (kendi) arkadaşlarının [hüsnüniyetini|iyi niyetini] [suistimal etti|kötüye kullandı].

reject.why: *Suistimal etmek* takes a direct object in the accusative: *hüsnüniyetini suistimal etmek*.

exercises.explain: Two izafets turned into words: *hüsnüniyet* (good faith) and *suistimal* (abuse). Everyday Turkish: *iyi niyetini kötüye kullandı*.

exercises.task: This note sounds stiff and old-fashioned. Rewrite it in everyday Turkish, keeping the meaning.
exercises.source: Toplantıya bilhassa davet edildiniz. Maalesef bizzat katılamayacaksanız, alelacele bir açıklama göndermeyiniz; bilakis, durumu hüsnüniyetle anlatınız.
models: Toplantıya özellikle davet edildiniz. Ne yazık ki kendiniz katılamayacaksanız, aceleyle bir açıklama göndermeyin; tersine, durumu iyi niyetle anlatın.
Toplantıya özellikle sizi çağırdık. Gelemeyecekseniz, hemen kısa bir mesaj atmayın; aksine, durumu açık açık ve iyi niyetle anlatın.
checklist: The long imperative `-(y)InIz` turned into everyday `-(y)In`: *göndermeyin*, *anlatın*
